notes: Twelve-directory roster approved by owner. Legacy thirteen-location claim not displayed.
Laguna Beach conflicting schedules are withheld; Seal Beach Saturday closing time requires confirmation. Seal Beach source ZIP omitted because it appears incorrect.
Location photographs incorporated at owner request. Santa Ana uses the current owner-supplied photo, resized without cropping. No generated restaurant scenes or promotional offers added.

locations.name: San Clemente
locations.hook: Make a day of Del Mar.
locations.reason: Stop for a family lunch or dinner on Avenida Del Mar. Our San Clemente chapter began in 2003.

photo.alt: San Clemente: White round corner tower, striped awnings and restaurant sign at Avenida Del Mar and Ola Vista

locations.name: Huntington Park
locations.reason: Come back to the beginning at the original El Ranchito, opened by the Avila family in 1966.

photo.alt: Huntington Park: Original brick storefront with teal awnings, mural, Mexican and American flags

locations.name: Corona del Mar
locations.reason: Make room for a meal in Corona del Mar, where the Avila family first opened a restaurant in 1997.

photo.alt: Corona del Mar: Brick corner tower with weather vane, orange awning, green window frames, palm and restaurant sign

locations.name: Costa Mesa
locations.reason: Try the handmade tortillas or discover the dishes María Elena created here, including Pepe’s Special.

photo.alt: Costa Mesa: Peach stucco entrance tower with burgundy awnings, green trim and palm-lined patio

locations.name: Foothill Ranch
locations.reason: Known for its grande burritos, this Portola Parkway location offers indoor and outdoor dining.

photo.alt: Foothill Ranch: Foothill Ranch exterior facade with large red and green restaurant sign and patio heaters below

locations.name: Laguna Beach
locations.hook: Add a table to your Laguna plans.
locations.reason: Make South Coast Highway your next lunch or dinner stop. Browse the Laguna Specials before you visit.
locations.hoursNote: Please call to confirm hours. The official website currently shows conflicting schedules.

photo.alt: Laguna Beach: Shingled restaurant facade and open bar window beneath a red patio umbrella

locations.name: Laguna Niguel
locations.reason: Explore the local favorites and kids’ menu, then bring your people to our table on La Paz Road.

photo.alt: Laguna Niguel: White stucco restaurant with red sign, terracotta roof, broad entrance arches and patio tables

locations.name: Lake Forest
locations.hook: Make time for a weekend meal.
locations.reason: Explore weekend brunch at the restaurant Sal Avila founded in 1997, now carried forward by his daughter Nathalie.

photo.alt: Lake Forest: Wide exterior with lush tropical planting, green walls, wagon wheel and stone restaurant sign

locations.name: Newport Beach
locations.hook: A family stop on the Peninsula.
locations.reason: Sergio brought Mama’s recipes to Newport Beach in 1975. Make this coastal chapter part of your next day out.

photo.alt: Newport Beach: Cream stucco restaurant with red lettering, arched door and open dining windows

locations.name: Orange
locations.hook: Choose something for the whole table.
locations.reason: Explore the botana platters and kids’ menu, then gather for a meal on South Orange Street.

photo.alt: Orange: pale-green church-shaped restaurant with tall shingled steeple, arched windows and front restaurant sign

locations.name: Santa Ana
locations.reason: Victor opened this restaurant in 1983. Its banquet rooms welcome birthdays, anniversaries and other family gatherings.

photo.alt: Santa Ana: Current restaurant exterior with red tile roofs, blue awnings, palms, a cream-and-terracotta patio wall and roadside Avila’s El Ranchito sign
photo.credit: Current photograph supplied by the restaurant owner

locations.name: Seal Beach
locations.reason: Find something to share from the botana platters, or settle into your own favorite on Main Street.
locations.hoursNote: Please call for Saturday hours. The published closing time needs clarification.

photo.alt: Seal Beach: Red brick Main Street storefront with large white and red restaurant sign, open windows and wooden sidewalk bench
